name: TX-26
label: Safe R

model.rationale: Brandon Gill is a well-funded incumbent in an R+11 district, while Steven Shook has raised almost nothing, and prediction markets give Democrats only about a 3% chance. The fundamentals point to a comfortable Republican win.
model.watch: A major late Democratic spending push or unexpected scandal could narrow the margin, though a flip remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-26 is a solidly Republican North Texas district where first-term incumbent Brandon Gill is seeking re-election. Gill has raised over $4.2 million and holds more than $1.4 million on hand, while Democratic nominee Steven Shook has raised under $20,000, leaving him little capacity to compete. No outside groups are spending against Gill, and no public polling of the race is available.

Prediction markets price Gill's chances near 98%, and the district's partisan lean of R+11 leaves Democrats little room. A Libertarian candidate appears on the ballot but is not a factor. The forecast expects Gill to win comfortably, with the main uncertainty being the size of his margin rather than the outcome.
